decisions.statement: The whole reconcile is run and what that reconcile would write is read.
The reconcile writes nothing, so a run of this leaves the index as it is.
A refusal names the file the entry is for rather than the entry.
An entry the reconcile would add is a file the index never filed.
An entry the reconcile would take away is a file no page names any more.
An entry naming a file no commit carries is judged by nothing here.
Such a file arrives and goes while the reconcile runs, so its drift is no skew.
The commit is read before the reconcile runs and again after it.
A file git says moved across that span is judged by nothing here.
Such a file landed while the reconcile ran, so its drift is no skew either.
A repository that never moved across that span is asked for no span.
The working tree is read before the reconcile runs and again after it.
A file written there and not yet committed is judged by nothing here.
Such a file is mid-landing rather than drifted.
A file whose own name says a page type stating it is mortal is judged by nothing here.
A mortal page is written and taken away as the agents run rather than drifted.
A drift outside that span refuses though the repository moved.
A missing page shows as an entry of its own as well as in what gathers many.
An entry gathering many files is judged by nothing here.
An entry the reconcile could not file is judged by nothing here.
Nothing here says why an entry drifted.
Nothing runs at change, because one file says nothing about the whole index.

definition: the check refusing an index entry that differs from what the pages say
